headline: Task force discussed opioid overdose data, needle cleanup plans, and harm reduction supply complaints.
summary: Partner organizations gave updates on substance misuse prevention efforts, including outreach, transportation funding, and recovery support. The group reviewed opioid overdose data, discussed a needle cleanup scheduled for October 17, and talked about needle exchange locations, safe injection sites, trespassing issues, and possibly accepting needles at Drug Take Back Day events.

1 | P a g e  
 
City of Nashua 
Division of Public Health and Community Services 
 
Mayor’s Task Force on Substance Misuse Meeting 
 
Tuesday, 09/21/2026 
9:30 – 11 a.m. 
Facilitator: Sakshi Gurung, Epidemiologist         Location: City Hall Auditorium, 3rd Floor 
Minutes 
 Partner Updates  
United Way  
• Gave information on the Wake for People initiative. Serving as the fiscal agent 
for Nashua Prevention Coalition. 
NH National Guard  
• Reported that another person has been hired to assist with strategic planning. 
Nashua Prevention Coalition:  
• Reported on the planning efforts to connect with young people in local high 
schools. 
Nashua Regional Planning Commission: 
• Reported on the funding for transportation/ride services for individuals 
receiving treatment and recovery services for opioid use.  
Nashua Community College: 
• Providing outreach to students who are struggling with recovery and 
addiction. 
Greater Nashua Mental Health Center:  
• Working on partnerships to support individuals transitioning out of jail and 
participating in Recovery Court. 
AMR Data 
• Slide presentation on AMR Data with information on opioid overdoses and 
opioid-related deaths.  
• Nashua data showed the lowest number of suspected overdoses through 
September. 
• Narcan use prior to the arrival of first responders was reported to be 
comparatively higher. 
• A five-year average comparison was provided. The most recent data showed a 
low number of overdose deaths. 
SSANA Update 
• Provided a comparison of transactions from 2025 to 2026. 
• SSANA discussed the October needle cleanup effort and how to safely dispose 
of discarded needles. Discussion on the need for volunteers to assist with the 
cleanup and appropriate equipment, including grabbers, gloves, and sharps 
containers or other approved hard plastic containers. Harm reduction staff are 
responsible for the cleanup protocol and will oversee the process. The cleanup 
is scheduled for October 17, from 8:00 AM to 11:00 AM. Approximately 100
2 | P a g e  
 
volunteers are expected to participate. The Mayor’s Office will provide 
volunteers with locations where cleanup is needed. DPW and Parks and 
Recreation may be able to provide appropriate sharps containers. 
• Needle exchange will operate from the parking lot of REVIVE. A suitable 
location is still being sought that is away from schools and daycares.  
• There was discussion regarding complaints about discarded needles and litter 
in areas where harm reduction supplies are distributed.  
• Concerns were raised that some individuals receiving supplies may use them in 
the immediate area and leave discarded needles or other materials behind. 
• The group discussed the importance of educating individuals who receive 
supplies about properly disposing of needles and respecting the surrounding 
area. 
Additional 
Discussions 
• The need for safe injection sites in New Hampshire was discussed. 
• Trespassing was discussed, including the challenges faced by the Police 
Department due to recent legislation. 
• The group discussed connecting individuals in recovery with appropriate 
mental health services. 
• Drug Take Back Day: The possibility of accepting needles as part of the large-
scale collection conducted twice a year was discussed. Discussions are 
ongoing. 
 
   
Next Meeting October 20, 2026
